title: Optional Catch‑All Routes
description: Make catch‑all routes that also match the parent path with [[...slug]].js for ultimate flexibility.

slides.title: The Missing Piece 🧩
slides.content:
# Double Brackets `[[...slug]].js`

A normal catch‑all route (`[...slug]`) **must** have at least one segment. `/blog` won't match `pages/blog/[...slug].js`.

Optional catch‑all routes fix this. Use **double brackets**:

* `pages/blog/[[...slug]].js` → matches both `/blog` and `/blog/a/b`.

When there are no segments, `router.query.slug` will be `undefined` (not an empty array).

slides.title: Optional Catch‑All (pages/blog/[[...slug]].js)
slides.content: Handles the blog index and all nested paths.

quizData.question: Which file would match both `/docs` and `/docs/getting-started/setup`?
quizData.explanation: `[[...slug]]` is optional, so it catches the base path `/docs` (slug undefined) and nested paths (slug array).

slides.title: Pre‑rendering with Optional Catch‑All 🔧
slides.content:
# In Data Fetching

Same concept: `slug` may be `undefined` or an array.

In `getStaticPaths`, you must now return a path for the **empty slug** as well:

```js
paths: [
  { params: { slug: false } }, // or [] — represents /blog
  { params: { slug: ['a'] } }
]
```

For the root case, use an empty array `[]`.

slides.title: getStaticPaths for Optional Catch‑All (pages/blog/[[...slug]].js)
slides.content: Notice the empty array for the root route.

quizData.question: In `getStaticPaths` for `[[...slug]]`, how do you represent the base path `/blog`?
quizData.explanation: An empty array signifies no path segments. That's the root of the catch‑all.
